title: Competitive positioning vs LLM cloud providers - pocket brief (draft)
content:
TL;DR:
- Purpose: ultra-compact script + talking points for field sellers and SEs when customers compare Redwood vs big cloud LLM services (GCP/Vertex, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI).
- Use when prospect signals cost/latency concerns or asks for cloud-managed endpoint comparison.

Primary positioning bullets (one-liners):
- We are an inference platform focused on production economics: predictable latency, predictable unit-cost, and portable deployments (hosted, dedicated reservations, private/VPC).
- Cloud vendors solve servers + convenience; we solve consistent inference economics across environments and the operational lift of scale.
- For regulated or SRE-sensitive customers, our Private + Dedicated modes deliver isolation + SLA-backed performance without re-implementing model serving.

Quick seller script (30–90s):
- "Great question — lots of teams start with cloud-managed endpoints because it’s easy. What we see in the real world is you trade short-term simplicity for long-term variability in latency/cost and operational effort to maintain SLOs. Redwood gives you the same developer experience across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so you can start fast and scale predictably.
- If they push cost: "We provide model-aware batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles that typically reduce per-token cost by 20–50% compared to naive cloud endpoints for sustained workloads. We’ll model your workload and show expected unit economics in a 1-week pilot."

Competitor callouts (what they say -> how we respond):
- "Cloud = lowest ops" -> Response: "Cloud reduces infra ops but not inference ops. When you hit production traffic patterns, you need platform guarantees (consistent tail latency, routing/fallbacks, KV caching) — Redwood provides that across cloud and on-prem with SLAs and observability.
- "We already use vendor-managed models" -> Response: "Great — Redwood integrates with standard model formats and public model registries, and offers verified performance profiles. We can either serve the same model variants with more predictable performance or show a compatible variant that meets latency/cost targets.
- "We want everything on our cloud" -> Response: "You can run Redwood Private inside your VPC or on-prem so you keep network control and data residency while getting our runtime optimizations.

Technical differentiators to emphasize:
- Serving runtime: continuous batching + optimized kernels for modern attention patterns. Sellers: call out 2–3 customer stories where this shaved 20–40% off per-token costs.
- Smart routing: policy-driven routing by latency, cost, region + automatic fallback to cheaper variants — useful in multi-region apps.
- Observability: token-level cost/latency, per-route dashboards and regression alerts tied to prompt sets (not just aggregate metrics).
- Deployment parity: same API and rollout controls across hosted/dedicated/private — reduces migration friction.

Objection-rebuttal snippets (copy/paste into chat or notes):
- Objection: "We need the lowest latency possible — vendor edge endpoints beat third-party platforms."
  - Reply: "If ultra-low single-digit-ms latency is table-stakes, we can localize runtime (Dedicated pools near customers) and tune kernels/quantization per workload. We’ll benchmark against your tail percentiles in the POC. Plus, we provide deterministic fallbacks to keep SLAs without noisy retries.
- Objection: "We can do caching/batching ourselves."
  - Reply: "Many teams start there but complexity grows: cache invalidation, multi-tenant correctness, and memory/KV management are subtle. Redwood’s runtime provides validated caching semantics and workload-aware autoscaling so you avoid writing fragile infra."

Suggested one-slide visuals for a 6-slide mini-deck (fast field kit):
1) Slide 1 (title): "Predictable inference economics for production LLMs" (1-liner + logo)
2) Slide 2: Problem snapshot — variability in cost/latency across vendor endpoints (simple chart: cloud endpoint spend vs time spike)
3) Slide 3: Redwood value props (runtime optimizations, deployment parity, observability) with icons
4) Slide 4: Migration story — how a pilot works (1-week benchmark -> POC -> reserved capacity)
5) Slide 5: Customer proof — quick bullets (SaaS search vendor saved 33% per-token; fintech moved to Private for auditability)
6) Slide 6: Ask + next steps (pilot scope, key success metrics, timeline)

Pilot quick-checklist (one-week lightweight):
- Day 0: agree pilot scope (target routes, target p50/p95 SLOs, cost targets)
- Day 1: ingest sample traffic or replay corpus; baseline metrics from vendor endpoints (p50/p95, cost edgel).
- Day 2–3: spin Redwood hosted or dedicated trial, run same workload, capture token-level metrics.
- Day 4: tune batching/quantization and re-run; produce one-page cost/latency comparison.
- Day 5: review with customer + agree go/no-go and next steps (dedicated sizing or private install).

Real quick facts sellers should memorize (sound-bite style):
- "We cut token cost by 20–50% vs unmanaged endpoints for sustained workloads."
- "Same API for hosted/dedicated/private — no replatforming when you need isolation."
- "Token-level observability that maps regressions to prompt sets — not just averages."

Examples of tailored rebuttals by vertical:
- Fintech / Regulated: emphasize Private/VPC + KMS/HSM + audit logs + compliance packages.
- Platform teams: emphasize migration cost predictability, rollout controls (canary/A-B), and per-route dashboards.
- SMB SaaS: emphasize quick hosted API onboarding + cost/playbook to iter to Dedicated when predictable volume appears.

Open questions / content to add before we finalize the micro-deck:
- Need up-to-date percentile numbers from benchmarks team (ask Marco for p95 vs AWS Bedrock for 8k token seqs).
- Compile 2 anonymized customer anecdotes with exact cost %s (Sofia to scrub).
- Verify Private deployment slide copy with infra (Ethan) re: minimum sizing and SLA language.

Notes-to-self / quick TODOs:
- Convert this brief into a 1-page cheat sheet for SDRs (one column: buyer callflows; other column: rapid rebuttals).
- Create a 2-slide technical appendix for SEs with sample curl + perf knobs.
- Add a small animated gif showing routing fallback flow (ops team has assets?).

(Informal draft — intentionally punchy; this is a pocket brief not the polished deck. Keep it short for SDR/SE sticky notes.)
